heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, synchronized video creation, and precise multimodal control across prompt, image, and script inputs.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected editorial hero with the headline anchored in the lower-left over a warm orange mesh-gradient canvas, while a layered media cluster floats diagonally across the upper-right: one large poster-style image preview, one smaller vertical video preview card with a play icon, and one thin storyboard strip underneath. Keep the hero visually premium and structured, not flashy—orange as the dominant accent, charcoal for contrast, and white text on a dark gradient overlay for readability. Add precise grid lines and subtle noise texture in the background, plus soft-shadow cards that lift on hover. Video should be a preview card rather than autoplay to maintain enterprise credibility and page speed. Ensure the composition clearly signals two products in one ecosystem: image generation on the primary visual and video generation in the secondary card.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is visual-first split with orange brand field and layered creative proof
Trust is kept early but as a slim editorial bar rather than a heavy proof wall
Product sections alternate between spotlight-plus-grid and accordion-with-visual to separate image and video models
A charcoal proof-led band is used only once to create contrast before testimonials
Pricing is presented as a comparison moment instead of a generic card stack
Testimonials use a carousel because there are 5 quotes, breaking the page rhythm before the form
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance for enterprise AI image and video generation. Create high-resolution visuals, synchronized audio-video, and cinematic content with a trusted Techjockey buying experience.

sections.backgroundTreatment: editorial split canvas with precision-line overlays and layered product previews
sections.designNote: Make the hero dynamic and product-first: strong headline, compact value bullets, and a right-side layered studio visual showing an AI poster frame, a video storyboard strip, and UI chips for prompts, motion, and audio sync. Keep the copy concise and highly legible against the orange field.

Use a restrained editorial trust strip immediately after the hero with the core capability chips: AI Image Generation, AI Video Generation with Audio, Multimodal Content Creation, and Enterprise-ready AI infrastructure. No logo marquee is needed; keep it clean and utility-led.

Break into two distinct product blocks with alternating visual emphasis. First present Seedream 4.5 as a spotlight section with a large preview panel and a supporting feature grid for the five capabilities. Then switch to Seedance 1.5 Pro using an accordion-with-visual or split-panel list to create contrast and emphasize motion, audio sync, and cinematic control. Avoid repeating the same card structure across both products.

Since the trust module is light, use this section to reinforce buying confidence through a compact grid of procurement benefits: guided evaluation, enterprise support, easy quote workflow, and fast demo access. Keep it more operational than promotional.

Introduce a deliberate dark editorial band here to create the strongest contrast on the page. Present the two product pricing cards or quote options in a side-by-side comparison layout. Seedance should feel slightly more commercial due to the visible starting price, while Seedream remains quote-led.

Use a carousel because there are five testimonials. Keep the slides visually clean and quote-forward, with role labels emphasizing creative authority. The tone should shift from product proof to buyer reassurance.

Place the lead form as a centered floating card to close conversion cleanly. Keep it friction-light and tied to demo or quote intent rather than a long questionnaire. This should feel like the final decision step.
If any media or partner strip is needed, make it a minimal footer-adjacent horizontal strip. Do not overbuild this area; it should feel like a quiet endcap rather than a new marketing push.

blueprint.designPersonality: A polished editorial creative suite for enterprise AI content teams: warm brand-led, highly structured, product-first, and premium without feeling flashy. It should communicate that ByteDance models can produce both striking images and synchronized audio-video output with professional control, while Techjockey provides a trusted buying experience.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium editorial-style hero visual showing layered AI creative outputs: a poster-like image preview, a short video storyboard strip, and floating UI chips for prompts, aspect ratio, motion, and audio sync. Include one gallery area with both video thumbnails and one image preview to satisfy the media requirement. Avoid sci-fi or neon aesthetics; the visuals should resemble a modern creative studio and enterprise content platform.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and product-specific, so 48px keeps it strong without breaking the layout.

colours.colourReason: The brand explicitly provides orange, white, charcoal, and light grey. To stay faithful to the brand and maximize visual identity, orange becomes the core CTA and highlight colour, with white as the primary canvas and charcoal for contrast. This keeps the page premium, energetic, and unmistakably Techjockey without drifting into generic AI gradients.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo lockup, large headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet-value list. The hero is text-forward with minimal media emphasis and no embedded form in the hero area.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Linear long-form landing page structure with a strong introductory banner followed by a lead-capture block. Visual rhythm is simple and stacked, with clear section breaks rather than deep nested layouts.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Form card and content blocks use plain boxed containers with sharp utility styling, limited ornamentation, and functional hierarchy. No evidence of glassmorphism, heavy shadows, or decorative card treatments.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is single-action and conversion-focused. Secondary CTA is not visible in the reference pattern. CTAs appear as isolated actions rather than persistent sticky bars.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module present in the reference layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference; no extractable footer pattern.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible area. Brand/logo image appears in the hero, while product storytelling is largely text-led. No discernible media carousel or large editorial imagery pattern is shown.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-first product sections with a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and stacked feature list. Structure supports progressive disclosure by introducing product value before enumerating capabilities. Multiple product modules can be presented sequentially.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed directly below the hero. Form is boxed, clearly titled, and separated from the marketing content to create a conversion-focused second step. Hidden fields and tracking-oriented implementation are implied by the markup.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utilitarian presentation with no visible motion system or animated storytelling pattern in the provided markup.
componentPatterns: bullet benefit list with icon markers
designNotes: Use a strong hero headline with concise supporting copy and benefit bullets.
Place the lead form as a separate high-priority module immediately after the hero.
Keep product sections modular and sequential for long-form scanning.
Use simple containers and restrained styling to maintain a B2B enterprise tone.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: add a gallery in the page containing videos one with image

mustHaveMoments: Single-screen hero with a strong value proposition and compact benefit bullets
Dedicated product comparison/segmentation between Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Media gallery featuring both video outputs and at least one image output to demonstrate multimodal capability
Lead capture/demo prompt after the hero to preserve conversion momentum
Capability blocks for image generation and video generation with clear, outcome-based feature summaries
Testimonial section with professional-role attribution to establish relevance for creative and enterprise buyers
Pricing/quote section with enterprise-oriented CTA phrasing
Final conversion footer with repeated CTA and reassurance copy
avoidPatterns: Overly decorative or experimental layouts that reduce clarity
Heavy glassmorphism, dramatic shadows, or flashy motion-first treatment
Long, dense paragraphs in the hero
Multiple competing primary CTAs above the fold
Persistent sticky CTA bars that feel aggressive for a high-consideration purchase
Form-first hero treatment that overwhelms product education
Generic stock imagery that does not show generated output
Deeply nested sections or complex multi-column storytelling that weakens scanning
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best approached as a high-intent lead-generation landing page for solution-aware enterprise buyers. The audience already understands AI creative tools, so the page should quickly prove that Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro solve real production needs: high-quality image generation, synchronized video/audio creation, and multimodal editing. A product-led narrative is the strongest fit because the offer is technical and capability-driven, but conversion still depends on trust. Since there are no logos or hard stats available, testimonial-first trust is the most credible strategy, especially with role-based quotes from creative and marketing decision-makers. The hero should stay split and text-forward to align with the reference pattern, while still leaving room for a compact media gallery further down the page to satisfy the instruction to include videos and one image. The overall tone should feel premium and enterprise-ready, with balanced section density so the page remains scannable across a long-form structure without becoming visually heavy.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
